dataset.name: US public timber stumpage & delivered price data (harmonized export)

suitability_and_limitations.suitability_summary: Harmonized, license-clean price observations for standing timber (stumpage) and delivered logs from six independent public sources, 1959–present, carried losslessly in their published units with a cited, swappable conversion to $/green ton. Suited to regional and temporal price-trend analysis, market research, and as an input to timber valuation models. Not a substitute for a local appraisal or a transaction-grade price quote.

application_limitations.statement: $/MBF is never scale-agnostic. Doyle, Scribner, and International ¼" are materially different volume measures; a flat MBF→ton factor across log rules produces errors on the order of 40%. Every MBF unit in this dataset is log-rule- and region-explicit (mbf_scribner_r1…r10, mbf_international_south, …) with a factor cited to USFS GTR-SRS-251.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable carries price_per_ton only, so a raw $/MBF cannot be mixed across log rules; in the full export, never mix rows whose original_unit names different log rules, and use price_per_ton for cross-region comparison.

application_limitations.statement: True volume→weight conversion factors vary roughly ±25% by species (aspen ≈2.3 t/cord vs oak ≈3.5 t/cord). The harmonized price_per_ton is fit for trend and cross-region comparison, not precision pricing or contract negotiation — use original_price/original_unit for those.
application_limitations.guard: for precision uses, read original_price and original_unit; tons_per_unit and conversion_source document the factor applied.

application_limitations.statement: Sources publish nested, overlapping region grains (statewide / peninsula / state_forest / management_unit, usfs_region / national_forest, district, land_office, multi_state_avg, state_avg). Aggregating across grains double-counts: Montana appears in a statewide feed and two multi-state USFS-region feeds; Cut-and-Sold carries both a per-forest grain and a region rollup of the same sales.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable keeps one region grain per source; in the full export, filter to exactly one region_type before aggregating.

application_limitations.statement: market_type separates stumpage (standing timber) from delivered (at-the-mill) prices; the gap is the full harvest-and-haul margin (roughly $40/ton for recent Montana sawlogs). They are different economic quantities and must never be averaged together.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable holds stumpage only; in the full export, filter on market_type (or price_basis) before aggregation.

application_limitations.statement: Public-land sale prices differ systematically from private-market prices (Munn & Rucker 1995, Forest Science 41(4):823–840): differences in sale size, road-building requirements, species mix, and sale format — not measurement error. ownership_basis is carried on every row as a transparency/control attribute, not a partition: combining across it is legitimate and often required, but should be a deliberate choice.
application_limitations.guard: group by or control for ownership_basis when comparing sources.

application_limitations.statement: Aggregates are volume-weighted only where the source publishes volumes (mi_dnr, mt_dnrc, tx_tfs, usfs_cutsold). or_odf and mt_bber publish no per-species volumes, so their aggregates are simple sale-count or survey means. ga_dor prices are weighted averages the agency computes, but it publishes no volumes, and pnw prices are carried as reported.
application_limitations.guard: in public_stumpage_comparable, no_volume_weights marks every row that carries no volumes, so an aggregate that includes it cannot be volume-weighted; exclude those rows or report them separately. In the full export, check the per-source candor block.

application_limitations.statement: The dataset covers only what agencies publish and a few surveys, so it is not a statistically representative sample of US timber transactions.
application_limitations.guard: do not generalize a dataset-wide level or trend to all US timber markets; name the sources and regions behind any claim.

data_quality_metrics: Licensed TimberMart-South/North rows are excluded by construction; a dbt test (assert_v_public_excludes_licensed) and an allowlist gate in the export script both verify it on every build.

Two independently derived series overlap for FY2009–2021 (USFS Cut-and-Sold PDF history vs PNW PPET, R6 Douglas-fir) and track within a few percent every year — validating the parsers, the Scribner conversion, and the volume-weighted aggregation.
known_gaps: No national-forest→state crosswalk: rows at usfs_region / national_forest / multi_state_avg grain carry state_code = NULL and are excluded from state aggregates.
No delivered→stumpage model: delivered-only sources (mt_bber) cannot yet be used as stumpage; price_basis is designed to carry modeled_stumpage rows but none exist.

Southeastern private-market prices are absent by license: the free state extension reports there are TimberMart-South redistributions, not public data. The public federal counterpart (Cut-and-Sold R8) is included.

stumpage.definition: price paid for standing timber, before harvest and haul.

delivered.definition: price paid for logs delivered at the mill (includes harvest and haul).

MBF.definition: thousand board feet, under a named log rule (Doyle, Scribner, or International ¼") — the rules are different volume measures.

green_ton.definition: 2,000 lb of freshly cut (green) wood; the harmonization target unit.

ownership_basis.definition: whose timber and how the price formed (public_federal_sale, public_state_sale, public_tribal_sale, private_survey, private_transaction_filing).

region_type.definition: the published geographic grain of a price row; grains are nested and overlapping.

weighting.definition: how a source's aggregate price was averaged: volume_weighted, sale_mean, survey_mean or as_reported (public_stumpage_comparable only).

context_and_definitions.methodology_summary: Each source is parsed from its published form (XLSX, PDF, HTML, API) into a typed staging table, harmonized in a dbt-duckdb medallion (dimension mapping via seeds, scale-explicit unit conversion cited to USFS GTR-SRS-251, stable hashed price_id), and published to a star schema whose public surface (v_public_prices) provably excludes licensed rows. Original prices and units are carried losslessly; every derived $/ton is reproducible from the factor on the row.
ethics_bias: The dataset covers only what agencies publish; states without an independent public price series are absent, which under-represents private timber markets, especially in the Southeast.
Prices from public-land auctions reflect public-sale characteristics and run below private-market levels (see ownership_bias).

target_audience: forest economists and market analysts
landowners and foresters seeking regional price context
researchers building timber valuation or land-use models
data engineers integrating price series into other systems
use_cases_and_target_users.recommended_expertise: Basic familiarity with timber sale terminology (stumpage vs delivered, board-foot log rules). The guards in application_limitations are the short list of mistakes domain outsiders make.
suggested_uses: regional and temporal price trends and indices
cross-source comparison with ownership_basis held visible
input to research models where a documented, reproducible public price series is required
key_instructions: Compare sources on price_per_ton, and read original_price only together with its original_unit.

Read public_stumpage_comparable for cross-source stumpage comparison: it holds one region grain per source and flags the rows to treat with care (is_lower_bound, is_unstable_snapshot, no_volume_weights).
Carry ownership_basis into any comparison, and filter the full export to exactly one region_type before aggregating.

provenance_and_relationships.review_method: Every source was web-verified against its publishing agency (catalogued source-by-source, with liveness and provenance flags); parsed values are reconciled against the reports' own printed aggregates where the report prints them.
provenance_and_relationships.candid_core_curation_method: Expert-curated: provenance is the decisive attribute (a free-to-read report carrying licensed values is classified licensed, not public), and caveats are named, specific, and machine-carried rather than folded into prose disclaimers.
related_datasets: TimberMart-South / TimberMart-North (licensed): the private-market survey standard for the US South and Lake States; excluded here by license, complementary by coverage.
USFS FIA Timber Products Output (TPO): demand-side mill-flow volumes on the same GTR-SRS-251 conversion basis; no prices.
provenance_and_relationships.comparison_notes: Public-sale prices here should be expected to sit below private-survey levels for comparable timber (Munn & Rucker 1995); the Oregon state-forest vs federal Cut-and-Sold gap visible in this dataset is the expected pattern, not a unit error.

lifecycle_and_access.support_status: actively maintained; sources refresh on their own cadences (quarterly to annual), the export refreshes with them.
lifecycle_and_access.curation_update_philosophy: A living dataset by design — sources get added, refreshed, and re-verified indefinitely. Reproducible versioned snapshots (manifest.json records each build) support citation; a frozen DOI-archived snapshot is planned.

ga_dor.name: Georgia Department of Revenue — Owner Harvest Timber Values

suitability_and_limitations.suitability_summary: Annual weighted-average prices PAID for standing timber in every Georgia county, in dollars per ton, computed by the state Revenue Commissioner from the timber sale and harvest reports (form PT-283T) that every private Georgia timber sale is required to file. Because filing is mandatory rather than voluntary, this is closer to a census of private transactions than to the sample surveys most private-land price data rests on — and it is the only source in this dataset built that way. Native dollars per ton, so no log rule or volume conversion is involved anywhere.

application_limitations.statement: The table prints 159 county rows but contains far fewer distinct prices: the Department replicates a small number of price zones across all counties. Distinct price vectors per year run 49 (2020), 31 (2021), 18 (2023, 2024, 2025) and just 2 (2026) — the most recent table is a flat North/South split. Counties within a zone are not independent observations, so treating 159 counties as 159 data points overstates the evidence by as much as eighty-fold.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable carries one row per DOR price_zone, year, species and product (county_fips lists the zone's counties); in the full export, group counties by price_zone or use region_type = 'state_avg', and never treat county rows as independent samples.

application_limitations.statement: The statewide rollup is a simple mean across counties, which makes it a county-COUNT weighted blend of the price zones rather than a harvest-weighted average. In 2026 it is effectively a 105-to-52 blend of two numbers. Georgia publishes no harvest volumes alongside the price table, so no better weight is available here.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable has no statewide rollup; in the full export, read the statewide figure as an unweighted county mean, and for harvest-weighted work pair it with county harvest data.

application_limitations.statement: The 2022 edition is missing and appears unrecoverable. The Department keeps only the current and prior year on its site, and the Internet Archive never captured that year's file. The series therefore runs 2020, 2021, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026.
application_limitations.guard: do not interpolate across the gap; year-over-year change is undefined for 2022 and 2023.

application_limitations.statement: These values exist to support ad valorem taxation of harvested timber. They are derived from prices actually paid, not set administratively, but they are annual averages and are not a substitute for a local appraisal or a transaction-grade quote.
application_limitations.guard: use for trend and regional comparison, not for valuing a specific tract.

data_quality_metrics: Built from mandatory statutory filings rather than voluntary response, which removes the self-selection that affects survey-based price series.
Cross-checked against an independent commercial survey of Georgia pine sawtimber for 2020-2025. The two agree within about 16% in every year, with this source averaging roughly 5% higher.
known_gaps: No harvest volumes are published with the prices, so nothing here can be volume-weighted.
Softwood and hardwood are reported as aggregates; there is no species detail within them.

stumpage.definition: the price paid for standing timber, before harvest and haul.

owner_harvest_value.definition: the weighted average price paid for timber harvested in a county, as reported on filed sale and harvest forms.

chip_n_saw.definition: intermediate-diameter softwood, between pulpwood and sawtimber.

price_zone.definition: a set of counties sharing an identical published price vector in a given year; recovered by this dataset, not printed by the source. In public_stumpage_comparable a zone is the counties that share one price for a year, species and product.

context_and_definitions.methodology_summary: The annual PDF table is parsed to one row per county and product column, counties are mapped to region codes, and a statewide mean is added alongside them. Prices are carried in their published dollars-per-ton with an identity conversion. Editions the Department has already removed are recovered from the Internet Archive.

target_audience: forest economists and analysts working on private-land timber prices
Georgia landowners, consulting foresters and county assessors
use_cases_and_target_users.recommended_expertise: awareness that county rows are replicated price zones.
suggested_uses: Georgia private-land stumpage trends by product, 2020 onward
a license-clean comparison point for commercial Southern price surveys
the North/South Georgia price gradient

provenance_and_relationships.review_method: published state table taken as published; county counts and product columns checked on every year parsed.
provenance_and_relationships.candid_core_curation_method: parse to county x product rows, label the recovered price zones, add an explicit statewide rollup.
related_datasets: The Department's Property Tax Administration Annual Report carries county harvested acres and assessed value from the same filings — the natural weight for a harvest-weighted average, not yet integrated.
provenance_and_relationships.comparison_notes: Expect close agreement with Southern commercial price surveys, and expect this source to sit slightly above them, consistent with a filing-based average that includes premium tracts.

lifecycle_and_access.curation_update_philosophy: refreshing ingest each year; older editions are recovered from the Internet Archive because the source keeps only two years.

mi_dnr.name: Michigan DNR State-Forest stumpage price reports

suitability_and_limitations.suitability_summary: Volume-weighted winning-bid stumpage from advertised Michigan State-Forest timber sales, quarterly, at Forest Management Unit grain — the cleanest machine-readable state source (published XLSX) and the Lake States' public-sale price benchmark.

application_limitations.statement: The $/MBF log rule varies by Forest Management Unit — Scribner Decimal C in most of the Upper Peninsula, International ¼" in the Lower Peninsula. A single flat MBF conversion across units is wrong; conversions here are unit-aware.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable carries price_per_ton only; in the full export, never pool raw $/MBF across FMUs, and use price_per_ton or check original_unit per row.

application_limitations.statement: Rows exist at statewide, peninsula, state-forest, and management-unit grain — the same sales rolled up four ways.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable keeps management_unit only; in the full export, filter to exactly one region_type before aggregating.

application_limitations.statement: Prices are competitive bids on state-forest sales (ownership_basis = public_state_sale); they reflect state sale characteristics, not the private Michigan market.
application_limitations.guard: control for ownership_basis when comparing to private surveys.

data_quality_metrics: Published as machine-readable XLSX by the agency; volume weights are the agency's own sale volumes.

fmu.definition: Forest Management Unit — the DNR's administrative sub-state unit and this source's finest grain.

scribner_decimal_c.definition: the Scribner log rule variant used in most UP units.

context_and_definitions.methodology_summary: Quarterly DNR XLSX reports ingested directly; winning bids volume-weighted to FMU, state-forest, peninsula, and statewide grains with FMU-aware log-rule conversion.
ethics_bias: State-sale price formation (advertised minimums, competitive bid) differs from private negotiation.

target_audience: Lake States market analysts and landowners
researchers pairing public-sale and private-survey series
use_cases_and_target_users.recommended_expertise: awareness of the FMU-varying log rule.
suggested_uses: quarterly Lake States price trends at sub-state grain
public-sale benchmark against private Lake States surveys

provenance_and_relationships.review_method: agency-published sale results taken as published.
provenance_and_relationships.candid_core_curation_method: direct XLSX ingest; dimension mapping via seeds.
related_datasets: usfs_cutsold R9 (this dataset) — the federal Eastern counterpart.
provenance_and_relationships.comparison_notes: Michigan DNR and Cut-and-Sold R9 are both public-sale prices but at different ownership (state vs federal) and grain.

lifecycle_and_access.curation_update_philosophy: refreshing snapshot; re-runnable ingest each quarter.

mt_bber.name: University of Montana BBER — quarterly delivered log prices

suitability_and_limitations.suitability_summary: Mill-DELIVERED sawlog prices from the University of Montana Bureau of Business and Economic Research's quarterly survey of primary wood processors ($/MBF Scribner), for Montana and USFS Regions 2 and 4. The dataset's only delivered-price source — valuable precisely because it is a different economic quantity than stumpage.

application_limitations.statement: These are prices at the mill, including harvest and haul — NOT stumpage. Recent Montana comparison inside this dataset: BBER delivered ≈$65/ton vs DNRC stumpage ≈$25/ton, a ~$40/ton harvest-and-haul margin. Averaging them with stumpage rows produces a meaningless number.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable excludes delivered rows; in the full export, filter to market_type = 'delivered' for these rows and never combine them with stumpage rows.

application_limitations.statement: Montana mills appear in the statewide feed AND in both the USFS R2 and R4 multi-state feeds — three overlapping region grains.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable excludes this source; in the full export, filter to one region_type (state_avg or multi_state_avg) to avoid double counting.

application_limitations.statement: A voluntary survey of processors with simple (unweighted) means — no per-species volumes are published, and respondent mix can shift between quarters. Small-sample quarters are noisier than the series looks.
application_limitations.guard: prefer multi-quarter averages; do not read quarter-to-quarter wiggles as market moves.

data_quality_metrics: Long-running survey by an established university bureau; the standard Montana delivered-price reference.
known_gaps: No stumpage equivalent is published; the delivered→stumpage conversion is an open modeling problem (no modeled rows exist in this dataset).

delivered_price.definition: price paid for logs delivered at the mill; includes harvest and haul costs on top of stumpage.

primary_processor.definition: sawmills and other facilities buying logs directly.
primary_processor.defined_by: University of Montana Bureau of Business and Economic Research

context_and_definitions.methodology_summary: BBER's published quarterly tables are ingested at statewide and USFS-region grain as survey means, flagged market_type='delivered', with the Scribner→ton conversion.
ethics_bias: Survey respondents are mills, not landowners; prices reflect what processors report paying, with voluntary-response selection effects.

target_audience: Montana and interior-West market analysts
researchers studying harvest-and-haul margins (paired with mt_dnrc)
use_cases_and_target_users.recommended_expertise: a firm grip on delivered vs stumpage.
suggested_uses: delivered-price trends for Montana and R2/R4
the stumpage↔delivered margin, paired with mt_dnrc

provenance_and_relationships.review_method: bureau-published survey tables taken as published.
provenance_and_relationships.candid_core_curation_method: ingest with explicit market_type and overlapping-grain labeling.
related_datasets: mt_dnrc (this dataset) — Montana stumpage; together the first independent public stumpage↔delivered pair.
provenance_and_relationships.comparison_notes: Expect BBER delivered well above any stumpage series for the same geography; the gap is the harvest-and-haul margin.

mt_dnrc.name: Montana DNRC — trust-land timber sale results

suitability_and_limitations.suitability_summary: Winning-bid sawlog stumpage in $/ton from Montana DNRC trust-land auctions, volume-weighted by estimated tons, at land-office grain plus a statewide rollup. Native $/ton (no board-foot conversion involved) and the stumpage half of the dataset's only public stumpage↔delivered pair.

application_limitations.statement: Ingested history starts FY2023; earlier sale results are available from DNRC only by request and are not included.
application_limitations.guard: not a trend series yet; use for current levels.

application_limitations.statement: Ponderosa pine is routinely bid at a nominal ~$2/ton floor on these sales and is deliberately kept as its own species rather than folded into the softwood aggregate, where it would drag the sawlog price down. Aggregates that re-combine species must handle it explicitly.
application_limitations.guard: exclude or separately weight ponderosa when building your own softwood aggregate.

application_limitations.statement: Non-sawtimber columns (firewood, biomass, pulp) are excluded from the ingest.
application_limitations.guard: no pulpwood prices exist for this source.

application_limitations.statement: Trust-land auction bids (ownership_basis = public_state_sale) reflect state sale characteristics, not the private Montana market.
application_limitations.guard: control for ownership_basis when comparing across sources.

data_quality_metrics: Volume-weighted using the agency's own per-sale estimated tons.

land_office.definition: DNRC's administrative unit — this source's finest grain.

trust_land.definition: state lands managed to generate revenue for designated beneficiaries (chiefly schools).

context_and_definitions.methodology_summary: Per-sale bid results are parsed from DNRC sale documents; rank-1 bids are volume-weighted by estimated tons to land-office and statewide grain, carried natively in $/ton.
ethics_bias: Auction prices on trust lands reflect mandated-revenue sale design; nominal-floor species bids (ponderosa) are administrative artifacts, not market valuations.

target_audience: Montana market participants and trust-land analysts
researchers studying harvest-and-haul margins (paired with mt_bber)
use_cases_and_target_users.recommended_expertise: awareness of the ponderosa floor and the short history.
suggested_uses: current Montana stumpage levels by land office
the stumpage↔delivered margin, paired with mt_bber

provenance_and_relationships.review_method: agency-published sale results taken as published.
provenance_and_relationships.candid_core_curation_method: rank-1-bid filter, tons-weighted aggregation, deliberate ponderosa isolation.
related_datasets: mt_bber (this dataset) — Montana delivered; together the first independent public stumpage↔delivered pair.
provenance_and_relationships.comparison_notes: Sits far below BBER delivered for the same geography (the harvest-and-haul margin) and is not directly comparable to $/MBF sources without a conversion.

lifecycle_and_access.curation_update_philosophy: refreshing ingest; history extends only forward unless request-only records are obtained.

or_odf.name: Oregon Department of Forestry — State-Forest timber sale results

suitability_and_limitations.suitability_summary: Realized winning bids from competitive Oregon state-forest timber auctions, by ODF district ($/MBF Scribner) — recent, sale-level, genuinely independent Western stumpage. Best for current Oregon state-sale price levels; not a deep historical series.

application_limitations.statement: ODF publishes no per-species volumes, so aggregated prices are simple sale-count means of winning bids, not volume-weighted; lo/hi carry the realized range. A few large sales can be under-represented relative to their volume.
application_limitations.guard: in public_stumpage_comparable, no_volume_weights marks these rows (a sale mean, with no volumes); in the full export, treat aggregates as a mean of sales and do not present them as volume-weighted.

application_limitations.statement: The source page is a rolling ~3-year window (deeper history exists only in per-sale prospectuses), so the series starts around 2023 and old quarters eventually drop from the upstream page.
application_limitations.guard: do not infer long-run trends from this source alone.

application_limitations.statement: Only the rank-1 (winning) bid is kept; losing bids and appraised minimums are excluded. Sawtimber only — ODF publishes no pulpwood prices here.
application_limitations.guard: this is a realized-price series, not a bid-distribution dataset.

data_quality_metrics: Magnitude cross-check against federal sales behaves as theory predicts — Oregon state-forest Douglas-fir bids run well above federal all-species Cut-and-Sold levels (better ground, single species, sale characteristics; Munn & Rucker 1995), not a unit error.
known_gaps: Pre-2023 history (PDF prospectuses only) is not ingested.

district.definition: the 9 ODF administrative districts — this source's finest grain, plus an Oregon state_avg rollup.

pond_value.definition: delivered log price at the mill pond — NOT what this source reports (these are stumpage bids).

context_and_definitions.methodology_summary: The ODF sale-results table is fetched and parsed; winning bids are kept, aggregated to district and state grain as sale-count means, with the Oregon Scribner→ton factor.
ethics_bias: State-auction prices reflect state sale characteristics and Oregon's coastal species mix; they are not a private-market benchmark.

target_audience: Oregon market participants and analysts
researchers of state trust-land economics
use_cases_and_target_users.recommended_expertise: awareness that aggregates are sale-count means over a short window.
suggested_uses: current Oregon state-sale price levels and ranges by district
the state-vs-federal price-gap comparison

provenance_and_relationships.review_method: agency-published auction results taken as published.
provenance_and_relationships.candid_core_curation_method: rank-1-bid filter; sale-count aggregation documented honestly as unweighted.
related_datasets: usfs_cutsold R6 (this dataset) — federal sales in the same geography.
provenance_and_relationships.comparison_notes: Expect state-forest bids well above federal Cut-and-Sold levels in the same region — a sale-characteristics gap, not an error.

lifecycle_and_access.support_status: active upstream (rolling window, updated with each auction).

pnw.name: USFS PNW Research Station — Production, Prices, Employment & Trade

suitability_and_limitations.suitability_summary: Annual average public-timber stumpage prices ($/MBF Scribner) for the Northwest from the PNW Research Station's PPET series, 1958–2022 — the longest clean Western public-stumpage record, ideal as historical backbone and validation anchor. A finished series: it is no longer updated.

application_limitations.statement: The 1958–2023 edition carries data only through 2022 and the series is not being extended. Post-2022 Western federal prices must come from USFS Cut-and-Sold.
application_limitations.guard: do not extrapolate; splice with usfs_cutsold for current values.

application_limitations.statement: Prices cover public timber (National Forest and state/BLM/BIA agency sales), not private transactions; levels sit below private-market prices for comparable timber.
application_limitations.guard: control for ownership_basis when comparing to private surveys.

application_limitations.statement: The source mixes two families at different grains: National-Forest sawtimber by species × USFS region, and public-lands stumpage by state × agency. They overlap in coverage.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable keeps the state-by-agency series (sub_state); in the full export, filter to one region_type before aggregating.

data_quality_metrics: R6 Douglas-fir tracks the independently derived Cut-and-Sold history within a few percent in every overlap year (FY2009–2021).

ppet.definition: Production, Prices, Employment, and Trade in Northwest Forest Industries — the station's long-running statistical bulletin.
ppet.defined_by: USDA Forest Service PNW Research Station

scribner.definition: the Western board-foot log rule; all $/MBF here is Scribner.

context_and_definitions.methodology_summary: Published Excel/CSV tables ingested directly (no PDF parsing); species × region and state × agency series carried at annual cadence with region-explicit Scribner→ton factors.
ethics_bias: Public-sale price formation (appraisal-based minimums, competitive overbid) differs from private negotiation; see the dataset-level ownership_bias caveat.

target_audience: researchers of Western timber markets and the historical federal harvest
anyone validating other Western price series
use_cases_and_target_users.recommended_expertise: awareness that the series ended in 2022 and covers public timber only.
suggested_uses: long-run Western price history (1958→)
cross-validation of derived series (as done against Cut-and-Sold)

provenance_and_relationships.review_method: agency-published statistical series taken as published; cross-validated against Cut-and-Sold overlap.
provenance_and_relationships.candid_core_curation_method: direct ingest of the official data files.
related_datasets: usfs_cutsold (this dataset) — the live continuation for federal prices.
provenance_and_relationships.comparison_notes: Where PPET and Cut-and-Sold overlap they agree within a few percent; differences are aggregation (calendar vs fiscal, species sets), not method error.

lifecycle_and_access.curation_update_philosophy: frozen historical backbone; no refresh expected.

tx_tfs.name: Texas A&M Forest Service — Timber Price Trends

suitability_and_limitations.suitability_summary: Annual volume-weighted average stumpage prices in dollars per ton for the East Texas timber market, from an independent survey of up to 60 active cooperators who report their actual sales. Federal timber sales are excluded, so these are private and other non-federal market prices. Pine sawtimber, pulpwood and chip-n-saw plus hardwood sawtimber and pulpwood, reported for Northeast Texas, Southeast Texas and an East Texas total, 2005 through 2025.

application_limitations.statement: The survey covers the East Texas timber market. Its "statewide" figure is a total across the survey's own two regions, not a price for the whole state, and most of Texas is outside the commercial timber belt entirely.
application_limitations.guard: read the rollup as East Texas; do not present it as a Texas statewide price.

application_limitations.statement: The two regional figures and the East Texas total are published together and nest, so counting both levels double-counts the market.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable keeps the two survey regions (sub_state); in the full export, filter to one region_type, 'sub_state' or 'state_avg'.

application_limitations.statement: The published dollars-per-thousand-board-feet and dollars-per-cord columns are not separate measurements. They are the per-ton figure multiplied by a fixed factor stated in the report footnotes, on the Doyle log scale. Only the per-ton figures are carried here.
application_limitations.guard: only the per-ton figures are carried, and public_stumpage_comparable has price_per_ton as its only price; do not reconstruct the source's board-foot column or mix it with board-foot prices from elsewhere.

application_limitations.statement: Where fewer than three sales are reported for a region and product, the source suppresses the price rather than publishing a thin average. Those cells are absent here rather than zero, and hardwood in Southeast Texas is suppressed in several years.
application_limitations.guard: expect gaps in the thinner series; absence is suppression, not a zero price.

application_limitations.statement: Annual summaries for 1999 through 2004 exist but are scanned images with no extractable text, so the series here starts in 2005. The 2005 edition reports hardwood sawlogs on a veneer-inclusive basis rather than the mixed sawlog basket used from 2006 onward, so hardwood sawtimber is absent for that year by design.
application_limitations.guard: treat 2005 as the first year, and expect no hardwood sawtimber in it.

data_quality_metrics: Volume-weighted by the source itself using reported sale volumes, so large sales do not distort the average — the report publishes the tonnage behind every figure alongside the sale count.

Cross-checked against an independent commercial survey of Texas pine sawtimber across 21 overlapping years. The two series correlate at 0.91 with a mean absolute difference of about 7%, despite drawing on entirely separate reporting panels.
known_gaps: Species detail within pine and hardwood is not reported.
Bimonthly issues carry more temporal resolution but no volumes, and are not included here.

stumpage.definition: the price paid for standing timber, before harvest and haul.

chip_n_saw.definition: intermediate-diameter softwood, between pulpwood and sawtimber.

volume_weighted_average.definition: an average in which each sale counts in proportion to the volume sold, rather than each sale counting equally.

cooperator.definition: a mill, dealer or forester who voluntarily reports completed sales to the survey.

context_and_definitions.methodology_summary: The annual summary table is parsed to one row per region, species and product. The survey's own volume-weighted average is carried as the price; its unweighted average is retained alongside for reference. Prices stay in their published dollars per ton with an identity conversion.
ethics_bias: Reporting is voluntary, so the panel is self-selected among active market participants, and its composition can shift between years.
Federal sales are excluded by design, which is what makes this a private-market price rather than a public-auction one.

target_audience: forest economists and analysts working on private-land timber prices
East Texas landowners, consulting foresters and mills
use_cases_and_target_users.recommended_expertise: awareness that the rollup covers East Texas only.
suggested_uses: long-run East Texas private stumpage trends by product, 2005 onward
a license-clean comparison point for commercial Southern price surveys
the Northeast versus Southeast Texas price gradient

provenance_and_relationships.review_method: published agency summary tables taken as published; the row count and section headers are checked on every year parsed.
provenance_and_relationships.candid_core_curation_method: parse to region, species and product rows; keep the volume-weighted price; drop the derived volume-unit columns.
related_datasets: The Georgia owner-harvest values are the other independent private-land price series here; together they bracket the Southern market with no licensed input.
provenance_and_relationships.comparison_notes: Expect close tracking with Southern commercial price surveys through the cycle, including the 2008-09 downturn, with year-to-year differences of a few percent arising from different reporting panels.

lifecycle_and_access.support_status: active upstream (annual summary, plus bimonthly issues).
lifecycle_and_access.curation_update_philosophy: refreshing ingest each year when the annual summary posts.

suitability_and_limitations.suitability_summary: Realized National-Forest sawtimber stumpage, derived as sale value ÷ sold volume from the USFS Cut-and-Sold reports — the only national federal price backbone in the dataset (all nine USFS regions, FY1977–present, including 134 individual national forests for FY1977–2023). Best for long-run federal price history and regions with no other public series.

application_limitations.statement: Since FY2019 Q3, Good Neighbor Authority sale volumes are included in the source workbooks without their values. Rows with value=0 are dropped, but mixed aggregates retain a LOW bias where GNA is heavily used — Regions 1 and 6 especially. The bias cannot be disaggregated at the published grain.
application_limitations.guard: in public_stumpage_comparable, is_lower_bound marks the affected R1 and R6 rows from FY2019 Q3; treat them as a lower bound, and trust trends more than levels there. In the full export, treat post-FY2019 Q3 R1 and R6 levels the same way.

application_limitations.statement: The same sales appear at national_forest grain (cs_r6_f01, …) and in a usfs_region rollup (cs_r1…cs_r10). Summing across both counts sales twice.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable keeps usfs_region only; in the full export, filter to region_type = 'national_forest' or 'usfs_region', never both.

application_limitations.statement: Single quarters are thin. The quarterly rows (FY2026 on) come from reports that are cumulative within the fiscal year, differenced into quarters, so one region-and-species quarter can rest on a single small sale (Region 5 Douglas-fir, FY2026 Q3: one 7.3 MBF sale). In Region 10 (Alaska), FY2026 Q1 sold-derived and cut-derived prices for the same rows diverge 8–30×. Headline figures should come from multi-year volume-weighted history, not a single quarter.
application_limitations.guard: in public_stumpage_comparable, is_unstable_snapshot marks every single-quarter row; do not quote them. In the full export, do not quote single-quarter prices either, and use multi-year volume-weighted averages.

application_limitations.statement: USFS reports on the federal fiscal year; FY Q1 (Oct–Dec) is mapped to the PRIOR calendar year's Q4 on the quarterly spine.
application_limitations.guard: when joining to calendar-year series, remember year/quarter here are already calendar-mapped.

application_limitations.statement: Prices are derived (value ÷ volume), not published as prices. Near-zero giveaway/option sales can produce prices of a few cents/MBF; they are real administrative transactions, not market prices.
application_limitations.guard: public_stumpage_comparable leaves out rows whose $/ton rounds to $0.00. In the full export, consider a minimum-price floor or volume weighting when aggregating small sales.

data_quality_metrics: For FY1977–2008, forest rows summed by product match each report's own all-forest total; sawtimber agrees within 0.5% in value and volume in every report that prints one, and the parser writes nothing otherwise.

Derived $/MBF matches each historical report's own printed $/MBF value-for-value (49 of 70,105 priced rows differ >2%, all at printed prices of $0.01–0.21/MBF where 2-decimal rounding inflates the relative gap).

Revised 2026-09-28. FY1977–2008 prices were re-parsed after two errors. Each report's state and all-forest summary pages had been filed under its last national forest, and its CCF pages summed with its MBF pages. FY2001–08 prices rose by a median of 45% (they had been about 31% low), and the last forest in each report now carries its own price. FY2009 onward is unchanged.

Revised 2026-10-11. Region 9 red and white pine (contract code R&WP) had been missed in FY2009–2021. Restored, Region 9 unspecified-pine sawtimber averages $119/MBF over those years, up from $89. Every FY2009-on forest-and-product sawtimber block now matches the report's printed total, and the parser writes nothing otherwise.
The FY2009–2021 overlap with the independent PNW PPET series (R6 Douglas-fir) tracks within a few percent every year.
known_gaps: The annual record ends FY2023. FY2024 and FY2025 are held only in a region-level report layout that is not yet parsed; FY2026 is quarterly, at region grain.
Two region-years are unparseable (scanned, garbled-OCR R3 FY1985–86).
No Region 7 exists (historical USFS renumbering, not missing data).

cut_vs_sold.definition: "Sold" = new sales awarded in the period (used here); "Cut" = harvest on previously awarded contracts.

good_neighbor_authority.definition: state agencies administering federal timber sales under agreement; their sale values are withheld from the workbooks.

log_rule.definition: Scribner in the West (R1–R6, R10), International ¼" in the South (R8) and East (R9), per USFS GTR-SRS-251 Table 1.

context_and_definitions.methodology_summary: Two machine eras are parsed: the current-quarter XLSX workbook (a refreshing snapshot at region grain) and the archived full-fiscal-year PDF reports FY1977–2025 (two report formats: TCS007 to FY2008, CUTS203F from FY2009), giving annual, sawtimber-only, volume-weighted prices at forest and region grain. Value=0/volume=0 rows are dropped.
ethics_bias: Federal timber sale prices run systematically below private-market prices (Munn & Rucker 1995) — sale size, road-building obligations, and species mix differ, so levels are not directly comparable to private surveys.

target_audience: researchers needing long-run (50-year) regional price history
analysts of federal timber program economics
use_cases_and_target_users.recommended_expertise: Understand value÷volume derivation and the Good Neighbor caveat before using post-2019 levels in R1/R6.
suggested_uses: long-run real price trends by USFS region
federal-vs-state/private price-gap analysis (with ownership_basis visible)
forest-grain price history (unique to this source)

provenance_and_relationships.review_method: Parsed values reconciled against each report's own printed $/MBF and, for FY1977–2008, its all-forest totals; overlap years cross-validated against the independent PNW PPET series.
provenance_and_relationships.candid_core_curation_method: expert-curated allowlist ingest; sawtimber only; both format eras normalized to one spine.
related_datasets: pnw (this dataset) — independent overlap FY2009–2021, ends 2022.
USFS ATSA reports — the same program's appraisal-side statistics.
provenance_and_relationships.comparison_notes: Region rollups and per-forest rows are the same sales at two grains; cross-source comparisons should use price_per_ton (regions differ in log rule).

lifecycle_and_access.support_status: active upstream (quarterly workbook); history frozen as archived PDFs.
lifecycle_and_access.curation_update_philosophy: current-quarter snapshot accumulates each quarter; history is parse-once.
